question_stem:
The Earth may be assumed to be an isolated uniform sphere with its mass of $6.0 \times 10^{24} \text{kg}$ concentrated at its centre.

A satellite of mass $1200 \text{kg}$ is in a circular orbit about the Earth in the Earth's gravitational field. The period of the orbit is 94 minutes.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Calculate the radius of the orbit of the satellite.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.part_stem: Rockets on the satellite are fired so that the satellite enters a different circular orbit that has a period of 150 minutes. The change in the mass of the satellite may be assumed to be negligible.
parts.text: Show that the radius of the new orbit is $9.4 \times 10^6 \text{m}$.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: State, with a reason, whether the gravitational potential energy of the satellite increases or decreases.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Determine the magnitude of the change in the gravitational potential energy of the satellite.
